title: Passé composé or imparfait?
summary: Tell a past story with two tenses: the imparfait for the background, the passé composé for what happened, plus venir de for the recent past.
focus: Choosing between the passé composé and the imparfait in a past narrative
content:
## Event or background?

French tells a past story with two tenses, each with its own job.

| imparfait (background) | passé composé (event) |
|---|---|
| what was going on | what happened |
| weather, time, feelings, descriptions | a single, completed action |
| habits: what used to happen | one step in a sequence |
| **il pleuvait**, **j'étais fatigué** | **je suis sorti**, **il a téléphoné** |

- **Il pleuvait quand je suis sorti.** (It was raining when I went out.)
- **J'avais faim, alors j'ai mangé une pomme.** (I was hungry, so I ate an apple.)

## Pendant que, quand and en train de

An action in progress is often *interrupted* by an event.

- **pendant que** + imparfait sets the background: **Pendant que je dormais, le chat a mangé mon sandwich.** (While I was sleeping, the cat ate my sandwich.)
- **quand** + passé composé marks the moment something cut in: **Je lisais quand le téléphone a sonné.** (I was reading when the phone rang.)
- **être en train de** + infinitive, in the imparfait, means *right in the middle of*: **J'étais en train de cuisiner quand Paul est arrivé.** (I was busy cooking when Paul arrived.)

Two actions running side by side both take the imparfait: **Pendant que je cuisinais, il lisait.**

## Signal words and verbs that shift

Some words point to one tense:

| imparfait | passé composé |
|---|---|
| **d'habitude** (usually), **souvent** (often), **tous les jours**, **quand j'étais petit** | **soudain**, **tout à coup** (suddenly), **un jour**, **hier à midi** |

A few verbs change meaning with the tense:

| imparfait (a state) | passé composé (an event) |
|---|---|
| **je savais** = I knew | **j'ai su** = I found out |
| **je connaissais Lyon** = I knew Lyon | **j'ai connu Paul** = I met Paul |
| **je voulais partir** = I wanted to leave | **je n'ai pas voulu partir** = I refused to leave |

## Venir de: the recent past

For something that has *just* happened, use **venir** in the present + **de** + infinitive:

- **Je viens de manger.** (I've just eaten.)
- **Le train vient de partir.** (The train has just left.)

| | venir | partir | sortir |
|---|---|---|---|
| je | viens | pars | sors |
| tu | viens | pars | sors |
| il / elle / on | vient | part | sort |
| nous | venons | partons | sortons |
| vous | venez | partez | sortez |
| ils / elles | viennent | partent | sortent |

**Partir** and **sortir** drop the **t** in the singular (**je pars**) and keep it in the plural (**nous partons**). In a past story, use the imparfait: **je venais de partir** (I had just left).

vocabulary.example: Tout à coup, le chien a aboyé.
vocabulary.example_meaning: All of a sudden, the dog barked.

vocabulary.example: D'habitude, je prenais le bus pour aller au lycée.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I usually took the bus to go to school.

vocabulary.example: Enfant, il allait souvent chez ses cousins.
vocabulary.example_meaning: As a child, he often went to his cousins' place.

vocabulary.example: Pendant que je cuisinais, les enfants regardaient un film.
vocabulary.example_meaning: While I was cooking, the children were watching a film.

vocabulary.meaning: to be in the middle of (doing)
vocabulary.example: J'étais en train de travailler quand tu as frappé.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I was in the middle of working when you knocked.

vocabulary.example: Je viens de recevoir ton message.
Ce soir, nous sortons avec des amis.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Tonight we're going out with friends.

vocabulary.meaning: to know (a person, a place); j'ai connu = I met
vocabulary.example: J'ai connu ma femme à l'université.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I met my wife at university.

quiz.prompt: Hier soir, il ___ quand je suis sorti.
quiz.explanation: The rain is the background, already going on when the event happened, so it takes the imparfait: il pleuvait.
hints: Weather as a backdrop to an event: which tense?

quiz.prompt: Je regardais la télé quand soudain le téléphone ___.
quiz.explanation: The phone ringing interrupts the action in progress, and 'soudain' flags a sudden event, so it takes the passé composé.

quiz.prompt: Tout à coup, Marc ___ dans l'escalier. (tomber, passé composé)
quiz.explanation: A sudden, completed event takes the passé composé; tomber uses être: Marc est tombé.
hints: 'Tout à coup' marks a single moment.

quiz.prompt: J'étais en ___ de cuisiner quand Paul est arrivé.
quiz.explanation: Être en train de + infinitive means to be in the middle of doing something.
hints: The fixed phrase is 'être en ___ de'.

quiz.prompt: 'Pendant que' is normally followed by the passé composé.
quiz.explanation: Pendant que introduces an action in progress, so it takes the imparfait: pendant que je dormais…
hints: 'While I WAS sleeping': in progress or completed?

quiz.prompt: En 2019, ___ Sophie à une fête ; aujourd'hui, c'est ma meilleure amie.
quiz.explanation: Meeting someone for the first time is an event: j'ai connu = I met. Je connaissais = I already knew.
hints: A first meeting is a one-off event.

quiz.prompt: In 'J'ai su la vérité hier', j'ai su means 'I found out'.
quiz.explanation: In the passé composé, savoir becomes an event: j'ai su = I found out. Je savais = I knew.
hints: Savoir in the passé composé means the moment you find something out.

quiz.prompt: Le train ___ de partir, tu l'as raté !
quiz.explanation: Venir in the present + de + infinitive means has just: le train vient de partir.
hints: The recent past uses venir in the present.

quiz.prompt: Elles ___ d'arriver à la gare. (venir, présent)
quiz.explanation: Venir de expresses the recent past, and the ils/elles form of venir is viennent.
hints: Ils/elles form of venir: double n.

conversations.title: Late for coffee
conversations.scenario: Hugo arrives very late at the café where Camille has been waiting, and tells her why.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Oui, désolé. J'ai eu une matinée incroyable.
lines.meaning: Yes, sorry. I had an incredible morning.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Je sortais de chez moi quand il a commencé à pleuvoir.
lines.meaning: I was leaving home when it started to rain.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Non. Et pendant que je cherchais un taxi, j'ai vu mon ancien prof de maths.
lines.meaning: No. And while I was looking for a taxi, I saw my old maths teacher.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Ah bon ? Tu le connaissais bien ?
lines.meaning: Really? Did you know him well?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Très bien. Il arrivait toujours en retard en cours, comme moi !
lines.meaning: Very well. He always arrived late to class, like me!

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Oui, une heure ! Soudain, j'ai regardé ma montre et je suis vite parti.
lines.meaning: Yes, for an hour! Suddenly I looked at my watch and left quickly.

lines.speaker: a

lines.meaning: Well, you're here now. Shall we order?

listening.text: Soudain, il a commencé à neiger.
listening.note: Soudain introduces an event, so it takes the passé composé.

listening.text: D'habitude, je partais à sept heures.
listening.meaning: I usually left at seven o'clock.
listening.note: A habit in the past takes the imparfait.

listening.text: Nous venons de sortir du cinéma.
listening.meaning: We've just come out of the cinema.
listening.note: Venir de + infinitive means have just.

listening.text: Il faisait beau quand nous sommes arrivés à la plage.
listening.meaning: The weather was nice when we arrived at the beach.
listening.note: New word: la plage = the beach.

listening.text: Pendant que les enfants jouaient, leurs parents bavardaient.
listening.meaning: While the children were playing, their parents were chatting.

listening.text: J'étais en train de lire quand tu m'as appelé.
listening.meaning: I was in the middle of reading when you called me.

listening.text: Elle connaissait déjà la ville, mais elle s'est perdue.
listening.meaning: She already knew the town, but she got lost.
listening.note: New word: se perdre = to get lost.

listening.text: Quand j'étais étudiant, je sortais souvent avec mes amis le vendredi soir.
listening.meaning: When I was a student, I often went out with my friends on Friday evenings.

guide.tip: Picture a film: the imparfait is the set and the music, the passé composé is each thing the actors do.

concept.title: The passé simple in books
concept.markdown: In novels and fairy tales you will meet a third past tense, the **passé simple**: **il entra**, **elle fut**, **ils partirent**. It does the passé composé's job in writing. At B1, just recognise it and read it as a passé composé: **il entra** = **il est entré**.

bites.title: Scene or event
bites.rule: The imparfait gives the background (weather, feelings, what was going on), and the passé composé tells what happened, one event after another.
bites.example: Il pleuvait quand je suis sorti.
bites.example_meaning: It was raining when I went out.

bites.title: Interrupted action
bites.rule: Imparfait (or être en train de + infinitive) for the action in progress; quand + passé composé for what cuts in.
bites.example: J'étais en train de dormir quand tu as appelé.
bites.example_meaning: I was in the middle of sleeping when you called.

bites.title: Signal words
bites.rule: Soudain, tout à coup and un jour signal the passé composé. D'habitude, souvent, tous les jours and quand j'étais petit signal the imparfait.
bites.example: D'habitude, je partais tôt, mais un jour, je suis parti tard.
bites.example_meaning: I usually left early, but one day I left late.

bites.title: Just happened
bites.rule: Venir in the present + de + infinitive means to have just done something.

sorts.title: Which tense does it call for?
sorts.why: Habits and background markers point to the imparfait; markers of a sudden, single event take the passé composé.

sorts.title: State or event?
buckets: an event (I found out, I met, I refused)
sorts.why: In the imparfait these verbs describe a state; in the passé composé they become an event: finding out, meeting, refusing.

spots.sentence: Il faisait froid et il neige quand nous sommes arrivés.
spots.why: The weather is the background of a past event, so it takes the imparfait.

spots.sentence: Je dormais quand soudain le téléphone sonnait.
spots.why: The phone cuts in suddenly. It is a single event, so it takes the passé composé.

spots.sentence: Quand nous étions étudiants, nous sortons tous les vendredis.
spots.why: A past habit takes the imparfait: nous sortions.

spots.sentence: Elle vient à partir, appelle-la sur son portable.
spots.why: The recent past is venir DE + infinitive.

spots.sentence: J'étais en train à lire quand il est arrivé.
spots.why: The phrase is être en train DE + infinitive.

builds.text: Nous venons de finir le repas.
J'étais en train de lire quand tu as appelé.

builds.meaning: She usually left early in the morning.
